title: A bill to provide for the authority for the successors and assigns of the Starr-Camargo Bridge Company to maintain and operate a toll bridge across the Rio Grande near Rio Grande City, Texas, and for other purposes.
official_summary:
(This measure has not been amended since it was introduced. The expanded summary of the Senate reported version is repeated here.)

(Sec. 1) This bill modifies the existing authority for the Starr-Camargo Bridge Company to maintain and operate a toll bridge across the Rio Grande River near Rio Grande City, Texas.

The authority, which currently expires 66 years after completion of the bridge (in 1966), is made permanent and expanded to include the successors or assigns of the company. The bridge must not consist of more than 14 lanes.

The company and its successors and assigns shall have the rights and privileges granted by federal law to the B and P Bridge Company, and may use eminent domain to acquire certain land needed for the bridge, subject to Texas laws and requirements for just compensation and public proceedings.

The company's successors and assigns may fix and charge tolls for transit over the bridge.

Those successors and assigns may also sell, assign, transfer, or mortgage the rights, powers, and privileges conferred on the company by the enacting law, to any public agency, to an international bridge authority or commission, or to a corporation.

Any such corporation may exercise such rights, powers, and privileges (including acquisition by mortgage foreclosure) as if they had been granted by the enacting law directly to the corporation.

summary.headline: This law makes permanent a federal authorization for a private company's successors to operate and charge tolls on a Rio Grande bridge near Rio Grande City, Texas.
summary.what_it_does: Before this law, the Starr-Camargo Bridge Company's authority to run a toll bridge across the Rio Grande was set to end 66 years after the bridge was finished in 1966. This law removes that end date and extends the authority to the company's successors and assigns. It also limits the bridge to no more than 14 lanes and lets the company use eminent domain for certain land, subject to Texas law and just compensation requirements. Successors may sell or transfer these rights to public agencies, international bridge authorities, or corporations.

who_it_affects.group: Starr-Camargo Bridge Company and its successors or assigns
who_it_affects.how: The company's bridge authority no longer expires on a set date, and successors can take over and charge tolls under the same rights.

who_it_affects.group: Drivers and travelers who cross the Rio Grande bridge near Rio Grande City
who_it_affects.how: They may continue to pay tolls set by the company or its successors to cross the bridge.

who_it_affects.group: Landowners near the planned bridge site
who_it_affects.how: Certain land needed for the bridge may be acquired through eminent domain, with compensation required under Texas law.

who_it_affects.group: Public agencies and international bridge authorities
who_it_affects.how: They may acquire the bridge rights, powers, and privileges through sale, assignment, transfer, or mortgage.
